title: VQ-VAE / VQGAN & Vector Quantization
interviewAnswer: Vector quantization maps continuous encoder features to entries in a discrete codebook. VQGAN combines discrete compression with perceptual/adversarial objectives to improve reconstructed visual quality.
why: Vector quantization connects compression, discrete representations and generative modeling, and it is directly relevant to tokenizer/bottleneck-based microstructure work.
intuition: The encoder produces continuous feature vectors, but the quantizer replaces each with the nearest learned codebook vector. The image is therefore represented by discrete code indices rather than full pixels/features.
deepDive: VQ-VAE uses an encoder, discrete codebook and decoder with a commitment/codebook objective; straight-through estimation passes gradients around the non-differentiable nearest-neighbor lookup. VQGAN adds perceptual/adversarial training to improve high-frequency realism and enables stronger compression. Codebook collapse/dead codes are common issues, addressed with usage monitoring, EMA updates or resets.
math:
z_q(x)=e_k where k=argmin_j ||z_e(x)-e_j||₂
Typical objective = reconstruction + codebook/commitment terms (+ perceptual/adversarial terms in VQGAN)
workedExample: A 256×256 image compressed to a 16×16 grid uses 256 discrete positions. If the codebook has 1024 entries, each index can be represented with 10 bits before entropy coding, which makes bitrate reasoning possible.
commonMistakes: Confusing the number of latent tokens with the actual number of bits required to encode them.
followUps: How do you measure compression in bits?
production: Track codebook version, utilization and bitrate as well as reconstruction metrics. Domain-specific tokenizers may outperform natural-image tokenizers when structural statistics differ.

lab.goal: Implement the core vector-quantization operation: map continuous latent vectors to nearest codebook entries.
lab.buildIt:
import numpy as np
z=np.array([[.1,.9],[.8,.2],[.45,.55]])
codebook=np.array([[0.,1.],[1.,0.],[.5,.5]])
d=((z[:,None,:]-codebook[None,:,:])**2).sum(-1)
idx=d.argmin(1); quantized=codebook[idx]
print(idx,quantized)
